submission.justification: Radiator-R2 at 3 cm thickness achieves the highest pion/kaon separation (4.627 sigma) at 10 GeV/c among all tested options. This maximizes the primary physics performance goal. 3 cm is within the allowed thickness range (1-6 cm). According to candidate_specs.md, Radiator-R2 satisfies the ageing constraint, with less than 10% transparency loss after a 10-year-equivalent humidity test. All constraints are met.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c.
requirements.evidence: Separation for Radiator-R2 at 3 cm is 4.627 sigma, which is the highest among all options.

requirements.requirement: The radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R2 is one of the candidates.

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after a 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test must not exceed 10%.
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R2 is documented to have less than 10% transparency loss after the required ageing test.
Chosen thickness is 3 cm, which is within [1, 6] cm.
